national.summary: Israeli voters are choosing their next government, with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu insisting only he can finish the job started eight months ago in Iran.
national.body: An oil tanker has caught fire after being caught in the Strait of Hormuz, Iran's navy said on Tuesday. "Hours ago, a rogue oil tanker that had switched off its tracking systems and was attempting to pass through a prohibited and unsafe area east of the Strait of Hormuz struck naval mines, sustaining damage and catching fire," the navy's public relations office said. "The Strait of Hormuz is unsafe and closed to rogue ships and vessels attempting to pass through without coordination," it added. The U.S. has urged shippers to use a southern route through the strait that Tehran regards as illegal.

national.title: DOJ asks Washington to set aside ballots from 400 alleged noncitizens
national.summary: Federal prosecutors said they sent a letter to the Washington secretary of state with a list of 400 people they claimed are not U.S. citizens.
national.body: Washington — Federal prosecutors in Washington state asked its top election official Monday to set aside ballots from more than 400 people who they believe are not U.S. citizens, expanding the Justice Department's efforts to call into question the accuracy of states' voter rolls just days before the midterm elections.Neil Floyd, the acting U.S. attorney in Seattle, and Pete Serrano, the top federal prosecutor in eastern Washington, said they believe that many of the more than 400 registered voters are green-card holders, who have legal immigration status but are not U.S. citizens and cannot vote in federal elections.Still, the prosecutors said that the suspected noncitizens have voted in multiple elections, and Floyd estimated that more than 1,500 ballots have been illegally cast."This is not the full number of noncitizens who have been voting in Washington," Floyd said. "This is only the tip of the iceberg."Floyd and Serrano said they provided Washington Secretary of State Steve Hobbs with a list of the 405 people who the Justice Department claims are illegally registered to vote and asked for ballots they may cast to be segregated until their citizenship status is confirmed.Hobbs confirmed his office received the letter from the Justice Department but raised concerns with the accuracy of the list. One of the roughly 400 records provided by the Justice Department in its letter is from 1994, he said, and more than 113 million primary and general election ballots have been cast since then."We take our responsibility to protect voter information seriously and will only respond to requests that follow due process. We saw what happened in California and don't want Washingtonians to be harassed," Hobbs said in a statement. He said the timing of the Justice Department's request, made one week before the Nov. 3 election, "is no doubt intended to cast unfounded suspicion on the results."The Justice Department sought Washington state's unredacted voter registration list last year. After Hobbs refused to turn over the information, the Trump administration sued the state in an effort to obtain the material, which includes voters' names, addresses, driver's license numbers and partial Social Security numbers.A federal judge dismissed the Justice Department's lawsuit last month. national.title: Florida mom left kids home alone while on trip to Vegas, deputies say
national.summary: The investigation began when a child called 911 reporting a dumbbell fell on her brother's head, deputies say.
national.body: A Central Florida mother is facing several child neglect charges after deputies say she left her four children home alone for days while she traveled to Las Vegas.According to the Osceola County Sheriff's Office, deputies got a 911 call just after 8:30 p.m. on Oct. 21 from a child who said her 9-year-old brother had been injured after a dumbbell fell onto his head.Deputies raced to the home and found that there were no adults present.In addition, four children, ages 14, 12, 11 and 9, had been left unsupervised.First responders also headed to the home and took the 9-year-old boy to Celebration Hospital for treatment.Mom said she was on work trip to Las Vegas, deputies sayDeputies said they were able to get in contact with the children's mother, who was identified as Irene Miller, and she told them that she was working in Las Vegas and was due to return on Oct. 23.Investigators said Miller had left on Oct. 18, and had a babysitter traveling from Tampa in the morning to get the children ready for school, and to check on them after.But, Miller said, the babysitter was not required to stay overnight.The 9-year-old boy who was injured by the dumbbell was released from the hospital, and the children's father was contacted and agreed to take them to his home.In addition, detectives with the Osceola County Sheriff's Office said they made plans to meet Miller as she got off her flight from Las Vegas at Orlando International Airport that Friday.Miller, 50, of Kissimmee, was arrested as she exited the airplane and was charged with four counts of child neglect without great bodily harm. She was also booked at the Orange County jail.

national.title: FBI raids California home tied to former Congressman Eric Swalwell - US media
national.summary: The California Democrat has faced multiple sexual misconduct allegations which he has denied.
national.body:
FBI officers raided a California home in connection with the investigation into former US Congressman Eric Swalwell, US media reports.

Swalwell, 45, dropped out of California's governor's race earlier this year and gave up his seat in the House of Representatives after allegations of sexual misconduct while in office emerged.

In August, the FBI stopped the former Democratic lawmaker at an an airport, seized his electronic devices and raided his Washington DC home as part of the investigation into those allegations.

Swalwell has in the past denied any wrongdoing and his attorney has called them "fabricated".

"These accusations are false, fabricated, and deeply offensive - a calculated and transparent political hit job," his attorney Sara Azari said around the time they were first reported.

The BBC has contacted Swalwell's lawyer and the Department of Justice for comment.

Swalwell has faced allegations from multiple women, including that he raped one victim while she was too intoxicated to respond and that he sent women unsolicited nude photographs.

national.title: Israeli police arrest man with knife near left-wing leader
national.summary: A man with a knife was arrested at an Israeli election event for left-wing leader Yair Golan as Israelis vote in a crucial election.
national.body: Israeli police arrested a man with a knife at an event for left-wing leader Yair Golan after what his party described as a "suspected stabbing attempt" Thursday, as Israelis went to the polls in a crucial election.As Golan mobilized voters Tuesday in Tel Aviv, "an unidentified man wearing a jacket approached him in a threatening manner," his party, The Democrats, said. "Golan's security guards blocked the man, and as they moved toward him, a large knife slipped from beneath his clothing and fell to the ground."The guards "immediately subdued him before he could do anything. Police were called to the scene and arrested the suspect."In a statement, Israeli police confirmed they "arrested a suspect in possession of a knife," but added that "contrary to reports, no attempted stabbing took place." Golan, an ex-military officer, is the leader of Israel's main left-wing party, The Democrats, which is made up of elements of Israel's once-popular Labour Party.He is in an electoral alliance led by former army chief Gadi Eisenkot, but sits further to the left.Golan is the only candidate for a major party in Israel still supporting a two-state solution with the Palestinians.Israeli police said that while they were escorting Golan, "officers on-site noticed a suspicious object protruding from beneath the coat of an individual standing near the public figure. The officers detained the individual for a search and discovered a knife in his possession."The suspect, who police say is a resident of Jerusalem in his 20s, was arrested and taken for questioning."Incitement and violence will not deter us," Golan said after the incident, blaming the incident on the "poison machine" run by Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. "I call on everyone who cares about security and democracy to go out and vote now," he added.Tuesday's incident follows a spat between Golan and the Israeli state. Golan said the security he was offered was insufficient."Only after a prolonged legal battle did the Shin Bet assume responsibility for his security, effective yesterday," his party said Tuesday, referring to Israel's counterintelligence and internal security agency."We don't want to imagine how this incident could have ended had it not been for the campaign the party waged that resulted in Shin Bet taking responsibility for Golan's security," they added in a later statement.

national.title: High airfares are weighing on Thanksgiving travel plans this year
national.summary: Average fares for the Thanksgiving holiday were up 31% in August from a year ago, according to aviation pricing data.
national.body: Some Americans are choosing to stay put instead of traveling for Thanksgiving, typically the busiest time of year for airlines, due to the high cost of airline tickets. Average fares for the Thanksgiving holiday were up 31% in August, compared to the same period last year, according to an analysis of the latest available data from Cirium. The spike in flight costs has driven down bookings for the period by 1.6%, according to the aviation analytics firm.Bookings to the following locales have dropped even more substantially, Cirium found:Newark (-24.6%)Seattle (-15.3%)Miami (-13.2%)Dallas (-12.6%)Denver (-11.6%)San Francisco (-11.7%)Rising jet fuel costs stemming from the war in Iran have increased airlines' operating costs. To offset those expenses, airlines have hiked fares, tacked on passenger surcharges and cut routes.Airlines have said they expect fares to remain elevated for some time even if the Middle East conflict subsides, noting that their fuel costs are substantially higher than they were this time last year. "It's expensive to fly airplanes," Scott Kirby, CEO of United Airlines, told Wall Street analysts in a conference call last week. "I think the tide has to rise for everyone or those airlines simply won't exist."Jet fuel represents airlines' second-largest expense after payroll costs, which have also risen under recently renegotiated labor contracts with pilots and flight attendants.

national.title: Truce begins in Ukraine city where residents ate weeds to survive
national.summary: The Oleshky ceasefire, which the White House said was secured by US First Lady Melania Trump, is meant to allow aid to get in and civilians to get out.
national.body:
A truce has begun in the Russian-occupied Ukrainian city of Oleshky, where residents have been trapped without food, water and electricity.

Ukrainian officials and Russia's defence ministry say the limited ceasefire is being respected. The truce, which the White House said was secured by US First Lady Melania Trump, is meant to allow aid deliveries and a civilian evacuation on Friday.

Oleshky, along the front line in the Kherson region, is trapped on one side by the Dnipro River, which separates it from Ukrainian positions, and on the other by Russian forces.

Many residents have resorted to cooking garden weeds to survive, telling the BBC they are suffering extreme hunger and want to leave.

There are concerns that the truce will not hold, with one resident saying: "I don't believe in Russia's humanity."

Up to 6,000 people, including 200 children, remain in Oleshky and its surrounding areas, Kyiv believes, with only 1,700 still living in the city itself.

Before the war it was home to 24,000 people, but it was seized by Russia during the first days of its full-scale invasion in February 2022.

Conditions have become so desperate that not only is getting supplies into the city extremely difficult, but escape is highly dangerous because the routes out of Oleshky have been mined and subject to drone attack.

national.title: Why it could be weeks or months before Israel's election winner is known
national.summary: The next prime minister will have to cobble together a coalition.
national.body:
Joseph Krauss, Associated Press Joseph Krauss, Associated Press

Polling stations in Israel will close on Tuesday evening, but it could be weeks before Benjamin Netanyahu or one of his opponents will be declared the next prime minister.

That's because Israelis vote for parties and not candidates. None of the several main parties is expected to win anywhere close to a 61-seat majority in Israel's parliament, known as the Knesset. So the next prime minister will have to cobble together a coalition.

Polls show a tight race between coalitions supporting Netanyahu and his main opponent, retired Gen. Gadi Eisenkot. In the end, both could fall short of a 61-seat majority, meaning another election would be held in the coming months with Netanyahu's government staying on as a caretaker.

Shortly after polls close at 10 p.m. local time (2000 GMT), Israel's three main television broadcasters will release exit polls estimating how many seats were won by each party.

The exit polls usually provide a good indication of how people have voted. But they also could vary and may not be borne out by the official results, which will be released in the coming days.

The Associated Press calls thousands of elections in the United States, but doesn't declare winners in foreign elections.

If, as expected, neither coalition pulls off a clear victory, then the coming weeks will see intense negotiations and bargaining among party leaders as they try to get to 61 seats.

national.title: Bolsonaro's Party accepts Brazil election defeat, but he refuses to concede
national.summary: Brazil's opposition party accepts Lula's election victory, but Flávio Bolsonaro won't concede, while President Trump calls the vote "rigged" without offering evidence.
national.body:
Opposition presidential candidate Sen. Flavio Bolsonaro speaks after the presidential election runoff in Brasilia, Brazil, Oct. 25, 2026. Eraldo Peres/AP hide caption

BRASILIA, Brazil — Brazil's Liberal Party, the party of defeated presidential candidate Flávio Bolsonaro, has acknowledged the results of Sunday's presidential election, recognizing incumbent President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva's victory. But Bolsonaro himself has yet to formally concede defeat.

The party's president, Valdemar Costa Neto, said in a statement Monday that the party recognizes the election results but believes "questions raised about the vote" still need to be clarified.

The concession came as President Donald Trump questioned the election's legitimacy, telling reporters Monday, "I didn't take sides, but it looked like another rigged election." Trump offered no evidence of fraud.

Bolsonaro initially said he would seek to annul the election results, citing alleged irregularities, including a last-minute extension of voting hours.

On Sunday, the Supreme Court ordered polling stations to remain open for two additional hours, until 7 p.m., following an appeal by Lula's campaign, which cited public transportation disruptions. Bolsonaro's campaign also requested an extension, citing heavy rain in southern Brazil.

In a video posted Monday, Bolsonaro shifted his approach, saying he would seek to have Lula's election victory disqualified over alleged abuses of political and economic power. "The law must apply to everyone," he said. "The competition must be fair and equal, which did not happen." Bolsonaro did not provide any evidence for this claim.

Bolsonaro also said Brazil's Federal Police had ordered him to surrender his passports after he visited his father, former President Jair Bolsonaro, in Brasília.

national.title: Norway and Finland leaders hold rare call with Putin
national.summary: This is the first time European leaders have had direct communication with Russia's president in more than a year.
national.body:
The leaders of Finland and Norway have held a joint call with Vladimir Putin - a rare contact between the Russian president and European leaders.

The aim was looking at "future negotiations to help to end the war" in Ukraine, the offices of President Alexander Stubb and Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Støre said. Their initiative was not on behalf of "Europe as a whole".

After the call, Putin said "confrontational" EU and Nato policies were prolonging the war which began when Russia launched a full-scale invasion in 2022.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky has spoken to the two Nordic leaders after their conversation with Putin. Last week, Zelensky met them as well as US special envoy Steve Witkoff in Oslo.

The Ukrainian leader said he was grateful for the "active support" of his Finnish and Norwegian counterparts.

Tuesday's 90-minute phone call was held from the Finnish capital Helsinki, and showed "big differences in views", Støre said.

Finland and Norway, which border Russia, initiated the call to "discuss Russia's war of aggression against Ukraine and the diplomatic efforts to end the war and promote peace and stability in Europe", the leaders' offices said.

The call was "frank and substantive", Stubb said, explaining that the war's outcome will "have a direct impact on our and the broader European security".

national.title: Discursive Verses: Jay-Z, the Super Bowl and playing with house money
national.summary: NPR Music culture critic and reporter Rodney Carmichael ruminates on the latest in rap culture. This week: Is the rap mogul's self-selection a crowning achievement or a final affront?
national.body:
It's no small irony that Jay-Z , the best personification of hip-hop's hopes and dreams, built his success by emulating America's worst excesses. Avarice. Greed. Domination. In turn, we idolized him for showing us "how to move in a room full of vultures." The streets he hustled in were made savage by design. The industry he conquered was out to vanquish him first. Indoctrinated by the same vampiric systems, we learned to praise those willing to sacrifice humanity — whether theirs or others' — in order to scale from the bottom up. The oppressor-oppressed dialectic can be funny that way. If you're not careful, you start to become the monster you're running from.

According to an announcement from the NFL, Jay-Z will headline the 2027 Super Bowl halftime show in February. He's reached a new pinnacle. Not the first rapper to play the halftime show, but the first act with the power to plug himself into that highly coveted slot. The gig even came with a $25 million paycheck, if you count the 2019 deal his entertainment agency Roc Nation scored to book the NFL's annual Super Bowl lineup. The game is to be sold, as the saying goes. And this time, a true player got to set the rules of engagement. After seven years of curating the talent — and pushing rap to the forefront in unprecedented fashion — he's poised to stick the proverbial feather in his Yankees fitted. Yet, hip-hop's response has been ambivalent. Some of us don't know whether we want to slow clap or slapbox with the god.

Whether it's viewed as a crowning achievement or the culmination of a deal that made Jigga the perfect "Black face" to whitewash the NFL's sullied image — per Colin Kaepernick's recent recounting (comments Jay-Z has not responded to) — ultimately depends on which version of the story hip-hop's most valuable hustler can convincingly sell. Like water to a whale.

Fresh off a PR crisis himself, Jay-Z's been engaged in his own rebranding campaign this year. It follows the recently recanted rape allegations made in a civil lawsuit that named Jay-Z and Sean "Diddy" Combs as co-defendants. (Jay-Z vehemently denied the allegations from the start and pursued a defamation and extortion lawsuit against the filing attorney, Tony Buzbee, which was also recently dismissed by an appellate court. Combs also denied the allegations against him and was sentenced to more than four years in prison on prostitution-related charges.) Surviving such a public smear campaign lent new meaning to the 30th anniversary of Reasonable Doubt . "We played enough defense, 2026 is all offense," as he told GQ's senior associate editor Frazier Tharpe in March. So he brought back the umlauts over his chosen name. He sheared off the Basquiat locs grown for both his daughter, Blue Ivy, and his deceased uncle. And he sold out Yankee Stadium three nights in a row.

national.title: A 'Green Army' is out to thwart El Niño flooding
national.summary: In Nairobi, a city prone to floods, workers in the "Green Army" are making preparations to prevent disaster when El Niño arrives.
national.body:
Nairobi is a city of rivers, streams and almost six million people.

For weeks, Kenya's bustling capital has braced for potentially catastrophic floods, as forecasters predict the strongest El Niño event on record this winter. Globally, this year's Super El Niño will likely peak in November or December and continue into early 2027. But Nairobi isn't just watching and waiting.

On a sunny October day near the city center, a team of workers in reflective vests shovels dirt and clears debris from the bank of a river. It's unseasonably hot — and hot days usually suggest there's an unusually strong rainy season ahead.

"The best thing to do is to be prepared," says Alex Oyando, a 30-year-old worker. "These drainage troughs are full of different things. When we remove the dirt, the water can flow — and it prevents flooding."

Nairobi frequently experiences catastrophic flash floods. More than 100 people died during rain-induced flash floods last March, and residents have pressured Kenya's government to do more to prevent these disasters in the future.

As part of the preparations, Nairobi's county government has mobilized the "Green Army," a youth-employment program of more than 4,000 people. While generally assigned to trash pickups and city greening projects, the workers have been out in full force to prepare for El Niño, clearing drainages and dismantling illegal structures like food stalls. These buildings are generally constructed by the community without government permits and are at an increased risk of collapsing during natural disasters.

Earlier this month, Oyando and his colleagues widened a drainage ditch that runs along a busy road lined with stalls selling clothing. Piles of fabric, plastic bottles and other litter often build up in the stream, triggering flash floods.

While the pay isn't as much as he could make elsewhere, Oyando admits, the shifts are manageable and not too grueling.

national.title: Key things to know about Israel's election
national.summary: After polls close late Tuesday, the jostling for power is likely to begin — between parties small and big — to achieve a governing coalition and name the next prime minister.
national.body:
Giovanna Dell'Orto, Associated Press Giovanna Dell'Orto, Associated Press

JERUSALEM (AP) — Israel's election is widely seen as a referendum on the country's longest-serving prime minister, Benjamin Netanyahu, and polling suggests a tight race with his chief rival, former military chief of staff Gadi Eisenkot.

Israelis, however, vote not for individuals but for parties, which then form alliances to create a majority coalition. No single party has ever won a majority in parliament, known as the Knesset.

WATCH: Netanyahu faces Israeli voters in first election since Oct. 7 and Gaza war

After polls close late Tuesday, the jostling for power is likely to begin — between parties small and big — to achieve a governing coalition and name the next prime minister.

Although it could be weeks or even months before a new prime minister is named, here are some key points we know as Israelis go to the polls.

This election is held against the background of the enduring trauma of the Hamas-led Oct. 7, 2023, attack, when militants killed 1,200 people, mostly civilians, and abducted 251 others, and the ensuing wars in Gaza and beyond.

The deadliest day in Israel's history featured prominently in the campaigns. Israelis have focused on the security failures surrounding Oct. 7 and the enormous burden on their society, rather than on the humanitarian situation in war-devastated Gaza.

national.title: Israelis are voting on whether to oust Netanyahu in first election since Oct. 7 attack
national.summary: Israelis are voting in a pivotal election Tuesday as their country wrestles with unresolved wars, continues to reel from Hamas' 2023 attack and is deeply divided over the character of the state and the right person to lead it.
national.body:
Tia Goldenberg, Associated Press Tia Goldenberg, Associated Press

JERUSALEM (AP) — Israelis are voting in a pivotal election Tuesday as their country wrestles with unresolved wars, continues to reel from Hamas' 2023 attack and is deeply divided over the character of the state and the right person to lead it.

Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who voted just after midday, faces an array of parties seeking to oust Israel's longest-serving premier from power. Opinion polls have suggested a tight race with his main rival, former military chief Gadi Eisenkot. Over 7 million people are eligible to vote, and tens of thousands have reportedly arrived from overseas.

WATCH: Netanyahu faces Israeli voters in first election since Oct. 7 and Gaza war

"This is a very moving and fateful moment," Netanyahu said. He told journalists after voting that he believes the Arab parties that could make or break the election "are receiving massive, truly massive, support. They are heading to the polls in unprecedented numbers." He urged supporters to forget about the beach or the barbecue and vote.

More than 31% of Israelis voted by noon, the highest voter turnout by midday since 1977, according to figures by the Central Elections Committee.

Inside Israel, the race is largely about security and who should serve to defend the country. Outside Israel, it's mainly about the country's reputation — and the security of Jewish people worldwide — after growing criticism over the war in Gaza and Jewish settler violence in the occupied West Bank.

In Israel's fragmented parliamentary politics, no single party has ever won an outright parliamentary majority. There is a chance that neither Netanyahu's religious and ultranationalist coalition nor the group of parties hoping to remove him has enough support for a majority. That could set off weeks of negotiations before a leader is declared.

Investigators have since released surveillance footage that showed him stealing a truck in the early hours of Tuesday morning. Officials realized Jacob Morley, 28, was unaccounted for around 11:30 p.m. Sunday at the Northwest Correctional Complex in Tiptonville, the Tennessee Department of Correction said in a statement.Investigators looked at security cameras and saw Morley escape while wearing his prison uniform, officials said. national.title: Mbappé sorry for 'ill-judged' Mao remark after backlash in China
national.summary: The France star had referred to the former Chinese leader as a "dictator" during an interview about memes.
national.body:
Kylian Mbappé has apologised for "ill-judged" comments he made about late Chinese leader Mao Zedong which led to him being dropped by several Chinese brands.

Mbappé had reportedly told French talk show The Bridge the meme "that makes me laugh the most, it's the one where there's a video of a guy, I think it's a Chinese dictator..." He then laughs as the clip cuts to a meme showing his face superimposed on an image resembling Mao.

The meme is part of a running joke about the Real Madrid forward being called a "dictator" because of his huge influence in football.

"My comment was ill-judged, and I now understand that it hurt many people in China and in Chinese communities around the world," Mbappé said in a statement.

Spain's La Liga also apologised, saying it "deeply regrets the offence that Kylian Mbappé's recent comments have caused among Chinese fans".

The joke did not go down well in China, where Mao is revered by the Communist Party, despite his chaotic and often violent rule that left millions dead.

A few people came out in support of him on Chinese social media, but that is a rare response given China's tightly controlled internet, where people are expected to toe the party and government line on sensitive topics.

Few topics are as sensitive as Mao, which may explain why brands were so quick to terminate partnerships with a global sports star like Mbappé.

national.title: New charges filed ex-FBI officials related to Hunter Biden probe
national.summary: The unsigned and unsworn superseding complaint comes just hours before the defendants are due to appear in federal court in Washington, D.C. for a preliminary hearing.
national.body: Federal prosecutors filed new criminal charges on Tuesday against two ex-FBI counterintelligence officials, accusing them of obstructing a congressional proceeding and lying to lawmakers about their roles in the bureau's investigations of Hunter Biden.The unsigned and unsworn superseding complaint, filed early Tuesday morning, comes just hours before the defendants Nikki Floris and Bradley Benavides are due to appear in federal court in Washington, D.C. for a preliminary hearing. At that hearing, attorneys for Floris and Benavides are expected to grill one of the government's witnesses to test the strength of the complaint and whether the Justice Department can demonstrate that there is probable cause to believe a crime was committed.The decision by the Justice Department to file a criminal complaint against two former senior FBI officials over testimony they gave three years ago so close to the midterm elections has raised eyebrows among former prosecutors and other federal officials. Criminal complaints in felony cases are typically reserved for more exigent circumstances, such as ongoing threats to public safety or national security. And Justice Department guidelines and norms have typically urged prosecutors to avoid taking overt investigative steps on politically sensitive cases so close to a national election.Prosecutors filing an unsworn and unsigned superseding complaint overnight is likely to raise further questions about whether the case is politically motivated."What is going on at the D.C. U.S. Attorney's Office? In the middle of the night, the government filed an unsigned and unsworn complaint attempting to fix the issues with their original charge against Ms. Floris and adding a new charge just as meritless as the first one," said Floris' legal team in a statement provided to CBS News."In our combined decades of DOJ service, we have never seen or even heard of something like this being filed," the lawyers said. "That's because the public lodging of criminal charges must be authorized by the grand jury, a judge, or the defendant herself. Here, the government has taken that power for itself in a desperate attempt to delay our client's right to challenge the charges in court and litigate this case in the media, rather than the courtroom. We have asked to address this outrageous government conduct against a decorated public servant at today's court

national.title: Nanotyrannus skeleton goes to auction in New York with £4.5m price tag
national.summary: The auction of the rare skeleton comes amid debate in the scientific community about whether dinosaur remains should end up in private hands or public view.
national.body:
The mounted skeleton of a newly-identified dinosaur once mistaken for a young Tyrannosaurus rex is up for auction - with a price-tag of at least $6m (£4.5m).

Nicknamed "Jodi", the roughly 10-foot-tall (3m) skeleton will be auctioned by Sotheby's in New York. The sale comes a year after researchers confirmed that the skeleton belongs to a distinct genus.

The Late Cretaceous carnivore is expected to fetch up to $9m when it goes under the hammer on Tuesday. The auction comes after Sotheby's sold a Tyrannosaurus rex, dubbed "Gus", for a record $50.1m (£37.4m) in July.

The sale comes as some in the scientific community debate whether dinosaur remains should be sold privately.

Sotheby's described "Jodi" as an "excellent exhibition-ready" skeleton with about 191 fossil-bone elements and a "beautifully preserved, virtually complete skull".

The auction house added that the Nanotyrannus is "one of only three such skeletons known to science." The specimen is the first to come to market since the existence of the genus was confirmed by US researchers last October, Sotheby's said.

Megan Jenkins, a palaeontologist at the University of Portsmouth, told BBC Radio 4's Today programme on Tuesday that Nanotyrannus "was for a very long time believed to be sort of a teenager of T. rex".

"But it's a lot smaller and its a lot more gracile. So it's very sort-of sleek, slender, [with] blade-like teeth for slicing through meat," Jenkins said.

national.body:
Chief football writer Published 3 hours ago Harry Kane has taken the scenic route to the Ballon d'Or - a road littered with doubts and diversions, but one that eventually led to the ultimate destination: being crowned as the world's best player.

The 33-year-old's glory at the London Palladium on Monday is fitting reward for an exemplary career that has seen records fall at his feet for England, Tottenham Hotspur and Bayern Munich.

Kane is England's top goalscorer with 91 goals. He has 125 England caps, joint-highest with Peter Shilton. He is Spurs' record scorer with 280 goals in 435 appearances. He scored a remarkable 73 goals in 65 games for Bayern Munich and England during the 2025–26 season.

This is the Kane of recent vintage, the world-class striker and complete footballer who beat Real Madrid and France striker Kylian Mbappe, as well as Spain's teenage Barcelona forward Lamine Yamal, to the sport's biggest personal honour.

Kane's humility has seen him described as an 'anti-superstar' and his achievement has been commended both inside and outside the football world.

One post on social media from Kane as he celebrated the greatest moment of his career said it all: "Work hard in silence. Let success be your noise."

It was one that started with loan moves around the lower divisions with Leyton Orient, Millwall, Norwich City and Leicester City before he developed into a great for club and country.

The same Kane sat on the bench on loan at Leicester City – alongside future England team-mate Jamie Vardy – when the Foxes lost a dramatic Championship play-off at Watford in May 2013.

national.title: Trump administration illegally fired James Comey's daughter, judge rules
national.summary: Maurene Comey believes she was let go from her job as a federal prosecutor because her father is the former FBI director.
national.body:
The US justice department illegally fired Maurene Comey, the daughter of former Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) director James Comey, a federal judge has ruled.

Comey, who lost her job as a federal prosecutor in New York in July 2025, sued the government, arguing she was unlawfully fired because of her father, a critic of US President Donald Trump, and because of her perceived political affiliations.

Judge Jesse Furman ruled on Monday that the Trump administration must reinstate her and that she must be given back pay.

A spokesperson for the justice department said in a statement that it disagreed with the decision and "will appeal in due course".

In his ruling, Judge Furman said Comey's dismissal violated the US Constitution as well as her right to a fair legal process.

He said the US attorney general can fire federal prosecutors but only "in a particular manner and only for certain reasons".

Furman noted that in Comey's role, "she was assigned some of the country's highest profile cases and consistently received the highest accolades from supervisors and peers alike".

Comey has worked on cases against the late sex offender Jeffrey Epstein, his accomplice Ghislaine Maxwell, and hip-hop mogul Sean "Diddy" Combs, who was convicted on prostitution-related charges involving his two ex-girlfriends last year.

national.title: Co-ordinated cattle raids kill at least 72 people in South Sudan
national.summary: The cycle of revenge attacks continue as the country heads towards its first election since independence.
national.body:
At least 72 people have been killed during cattle raids in South Sudan's northern Warrap state, according to the regional government.

An unspecified number of cattle were taken and homes burnt during what was a "co-ordinated attack" on Monday involving two communities in Tonj North county, the state authorities said.

Such deadly violence is often part of a cycle of revenge attacks as cattle are a main source of wealth and pride for many communities and are also important as young men need them as dowries to get married.

Clashes over territory are also common across the country as it prepares to hold its first election since its independence in 2011 - delayed because of a brutal civil war.

The clashes occurred near the border of Warrap and Unity states in the area of Akop Payam, with some members from Lou Ariik community said to have attacked those from Apuk Padoch community.

William Wol Mayom Bol, Warrap state's information minister, said they followed deadly violence last Friday that claimed eight lives.

The state governor, Angelo Ngot Mayar, sent his condolences to bereaved families and directed security agencies to evacuate the wounded.

He said efforts were under way recover the cattle and find those behind the assault.

national.summary: Greenhouse gas concentrations in the atmosphere rose to record highs in 2025, locking in climate​ impacts that will persist for centuries, the U.N. says.
national.body: Geneva — Greenhouse gas concentrations in the atmosphere rose to record highs in 2025, locking in climate impacts that will persist for centuries, the United Nations said on Tuesday. Levels of the three main greenhouse gases -- the climate-warming carbon dioxide, methane and nitrous oxide -- all rose to unprecedented figures in 2025, the U.N.'s weather and climate agency said. The World Meteorological Organization said the rise would lead to more long-term temperature increases for the planet. The WMO's 22nd annual Greenhouse Gas Bulletin comes ahead of the COP31 U.N. climate summit in Antalya, Turkey, from Nov. 9 to Nov. 20. "Another year, another new record," said WMO Deputy Secretary-General Ko Barrett. "Greenhouse gases are trapping an unprecedented amount of heat in the atmosphere, providing energy for more extreme weather and associated risks to our economies and societies. "The past 11 years have been the warmest on record and this trend is set to continue. Carbon dioxide (CO2) has a very long life-time and so will affect the global climate not just for years but for decades and even centuries."El Nino's impactThe bulletin looks at greenhouse gas concentrations -- the amount of those gases in the atmosphere -- rather than new annual emissions amounts as the world burns more coal, oil and gas. In 2025, carbon dioxide concentrations were at 426.8 parts per million (ppm); methane at 1,948 parts per billion, and nitrous oxide at 339.1 parts per billion. That takes them, respectively, to 153%, 267% and 126% of the pre-industrial levels witnessed before 1750. Of the three major greenhouse gases, CO2 accounts for about 66% of the warming effect on the climate. Around half of the total CO2 emitted each year remains in the atmosphere; the rest is absorbed by the land and oceans. From 2024 to 2025, the global average concentration of CO2 rose by 2.8 ppm -- smaller than the record surge from 2023 to 2024 of 3.6 ppm. WMO senior scientific officer Oksana Tarasova said this reflected the "recovery of the land carbon sinks and reduced fire carbon emissions in 2025 after the strong 2023/2024 El Nino," the naturally occurring, climate-warming weather phenomenon. "However, a 2.8 ppm annual increase is still a substantial addition of carbon to the atmosphere from fossil fuel burning." national.title: Ex-FBI chief James Comey faces federal charges for third time
national.summary: Comey's lawyers say the case stems from alleged disclosure of classified information to the New York Times in 2016.
national.body:
Federal prosecutors have taken steps to charge ex-Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) Director James Comey with leaking national defence information, according to a court filing.

It marks the third time the justice department has moved to bring criminal charges against Comey, a longtime critic of President Donald Trump.

Few details are provided about the two counts in the three-page filing, but Comey's lawyers said in separate court papers that the case stemmed from an alleged disclosure of classified information to the New York Times in October 2016, while he was head of the FBI.

Comey denied any wrongdoing in a video posted on Substack on Monday, calling the charges an "appalling abuse".

"It would almost be funny if it weren't such an appalling abuse of the department of justice, one that we cannot become numb to," he said in the clip.

"Nothing's changed with me - I'm still innocent, I'm still not afraid of these people and I still believe in the independent federal judiciary."

Comey was charged in Washington DC through a criminal information, which is a formal written charging document filed directly by a prosecutor.

This is different to a criminal indictment, which must be approved by a grand jury, a group of citizens sworn in to review if evidence is strong enough to prosecute.

national.summary: A Dutch broadcaster reverses a decision to take part, citing "sensitivities" over Israel's participation.
national.body:
The Netherlands has pulled out of next year's Eurovision Song Contest, with public broadcaster NPO citing "sensitivities" over Israel's participation - reversing a previous decision to take part.

The Netherlands and four other countries boycotted this year's event, after Dutch network Avrotros pulled out.

Avrotros said it would also not take part next year, but NPO, which oversees public broadcasting in the country, stepped in and pledged last month that the country would return in 2027 .

However, NPO's media director Jurre Bosman said on Tuesday that "Israel's participation elicits various reactions in society and causes discussion and division", and NPO "has decided to forgo participation in 2027".

NPO chair Jet de Ranitz said the organisation had held discussions with broadcasters about participating next year.

"In those discussions, we initially felt there was sufficient support to return. Unfortunately, we were unable to find a suitable format for this.

"As a result, we must conclude that it is currently too early to participate in the Eurovision Song Contest in 2027.

"Due to the sensitivities surrounding the themes currently at play, we have decided to take a step back for the time being."

national.title: Turnout so far highest on record as Israelis vote in pivotal election
national.summary: The elections - the first since the Hamas-led attacks on Israel and the wars which followed - are widely seen as a referendum on Benjamin Netanyahu.
national.body:
Turnout so far is at record levels, as Israelis vote in what many view as one of the most pivotal elections in the country's history.

Polling published on Friday suggests incumbent Benjamin Netanyahu is almost neck-and-neck with former military chief Gadi Eisenkot in the race to become prime minister.

But neither of their political blocs are projected to win the 61 seats needed to form a majority government - meaning weeks or months of political wrangling may lie ahead.

The campaign has been shaped by the issues of democracy and security, and the election is widely being seen as a referendum on Netanyahu's rule.

Many leading parties complained on Tuesday morning of alleged irregularities at polling stations across the country - but Israel's Central Election Committee (CEC) says there is no evidence of systematic tampering with ballot slips.

Israel's proportional representation system means governments have always been coalitions - and the race to power can, and has, produced unexpected alliances. But this election looks especially tight - and lines in the sand have already been drawn.

Eisenkot, who leads the newly formed Yashar Party, is the main figure in the so-called "change bloc", a collection of parties who have ideological differences but share the goal of ousting Netanyahu.

Other leaders in the bloc include former prime minister Naftali Bennett and Avigdor Lieberman - both right-wingers who take hardline positions on security - and Yair Golan, a left-leaning former general.

national.title: U.K. charges 2 men linked to alleged terror plot against air base
national.summary: Two men arrested in connection with the alleged Iran-linked terror plot targeting RAF Fairford in England have been charged with national security offenses.
national.body: London — Two men have been charged with serious security offenses in Britain after being arrested in connection with the incident last month near RAF Fairford, the air base in England that had been used by the U.S. military to launch strikes on Iran, the U.K. Crown Prosecution Service (CPS) said Tuesday.Mohmed Abdulkarim, 24, and Nouman Essghir, 24, both British nationals and London residents, were charged under the 2023 National Security Act. Abdulkarim was charged with "assisting a foreign intelligence service" in September and "engaging in conduct that was likely to materially assist a foreign intelligence service in carrying out U.K.-related activities."The CPS said Essghir was charged with a national security offense after he "approached or was in the vicinity of a prohibited place and his conduct was for a purpose that he knew, or having regards to other matters known to him ought reasonably to have known, was prejudicial to the safety or interests of the United Kingdom."Both men were arrested last week on suspicion of assisting Iran's intelligence service in a suspected plot targeting the Fairford air base in England. Abdulkarim was arrested by Counter Terror Police under the National Security Act last week, along with another 25-year-old man — a British-Iranian dual national who was released on bail pending further investigation.Police are still investigating a suspected terror plot against Fairford after five men were initially detained on Sept. 27 near the base in western England. All five of those men were also released on bail, but police said they remained under investigation and would be monitored.U.K. Prime Minister Andy Burnham has said the government believes Iran "played a part" in the incident at the base, which prompted the U.S. Air Force to remove all of its B-1 bombers from RAF Fairford. The base had been home to U.S. long-range bombers for many years, and it was used during the war with Iran to launch strikes on the Islamic Republic. Residents of a nearby town were evacuated from their homes near the base as armed police and bomb-disposal experts searched the area on Sept. 27. They found gasoline in three vans that had been driven by the five initial suspects, parked close to an entrance to the base, but no explosives.Iranian officials have said repeatedly that any bases used to attack the country would be considered legitimate targets

national.summary: The German-owned chain's low prices are winning over shoppers — and pushing competitors to respond.
national.body:
In the summer of 2020, I lived briefly in Ithaca, New York. It's the only time I've lived near Aldi, the grocery store known for low prices. I went twice, and I thought it was fine, but underwhelming. I appreciated the low prices, but it didn't have everything I needed. The store was small and a bit shabby.

I didn't know it yet, but those are the exact ingredients that have made Aldi the fastest-growing grocery chain in America. Per Bloomberg , Aldi plans to have more than 3,000 American locations by the end of 2028, which would be more than any other chain but Walmart. In 2024, Aldi generated some $29 billion in U.S. sales, which is more than Trader Joe's.

Aldi is a German company known for having low, low prices, and it deserves that reputation. Food reporter Deena Shanker told me that her experience comparison shopping over many months was that Aldi either matched Walmart on price or was a bit cheaper. Grocers like Wegmans and Kroger have announced defensive price reductions, and an analysis published in late 2023 of Lidl, another German grocer with a very similar model to Aldi's but fewer U.S. stores, found that grocery chains reduced their markups ~7 percent in areas where Lidl stores opened .

All to say: Aldi is disrupting the grocery business and actually lowering prices even as the cost of food—at restaurants and other grocery stores—goes up and up.

Maybe this sounds a bit humdrum. But I found it totally intriguing and perplexing, because…

One necessary but not sufficient explanation for Aldi's low prices is that management is obsessed with efficiency and cutting unnecessary costs. There's no music in stores, because speakers (and licensing fees for muzak) cost money. The staff places products on shelves still in the cardboard boxes they were trucked in on, because artfully unpacking fruits, bread, and jerky sticks would mean higher labor costs. The shabbiness is intentional — it's the cost of cheaper groceries.

But other grocery chains are similarly obsessed with efficiency. Apple said it was aware of "an issue impacting the inner display on a small number" of the phones and urged affected users to contact the company for a replacement.

The Duo's launch, which attracted crowds at Apple stores around the world last week, is an attempt to reinvigorate the brand's device range and challenge the foldable phones made by rivals.

Some Duo owners also posted photos online showing cracks along the screen's centre crease, while others reported a crunching noise when opening the device.

An iPhone Duo user, Justin Lokos, posted an image of a device with lines across the right side of the display and later uploaded a picture of a new handset alongside the broken one, thanking an Apple store in New York for its help.

In a news release issued Tuesday, Dunkirk Hospitality, LLC, owner of the former EconoLodge in Fredonia, now America’s Best Value Inn, countered statements by the
local.body:
A hotel owner is responding to comments made recently by Fredonia Mayor Michael Ferguson while planning a lawsuit regarding the situation.

In a news release issued Tuesday, Dunkirk Hospitality, LLC, owner of the former EconoLodge in Fredonia, now America's Best Value Inn, countered statements by the village leader and served an Amended Notice of Claim on the municipality.

Ferguson told the OBSERVER, "Burn me once, shame on you. Burn me twice, shame on me," but that worry rests on informal conversations. The parties never signed a contract or put any obligation in writing.

"Instead of worrying about burning himself, he should be worrying about burning the village," stated Richard J. Morrisroe, Esq., of VanDette Law PLLC, counsel for Dunkirk Hospitality. "Ferguson could have avoided the improper handling of the hotel and the litigation that will follow. Taxpayers will feel the burn as well."

Morrisroe continued: "It is surprising that Mayor Ferguson worries so much about this business, being that he comes from the private sector. He should know that the mayor does not control the supply and demand of hotel occupancy. He should also know that everyone is entitled to due process rights, including business owners such as hotel operator Dunkirk Hospitality LLC."

The notice alleges the village ordered every occupant out on April 27, days after inspections, without notice or a hearing, then rescinded the order June 16 after the hotel won a temporary restraining order. It alleges the village's own inspector found no violations on Sept. 9, and on Sept. 21 the Village certified the hotel's roof replacement as substantially compliant.

"The same village that called the roof 'collapsing' in April certified the replacement work in September," Morrisroe argued. "The notice demands the village's proof."

The notice alleges a pretext: the village used the closure to remove county placements and keep them out. "By his own account, the Mayor 'worked hard to get' that programming removed and expressed 'strong resistance' to its return, even as he acknowledges cold weather means people will need emergency housing," Morrisroe said. "My client did not create the nuisance issues he raises. A hotel is not responsible for policing the nuisance or alleged criminal behavior of guests placed by Chautauqua County DSS, just as a landlord is not responsible for policing its tenants."

The Village of Fredonia Office of Emergency Management, in coordination with the village’s water treatment plant and the Chautauqua County Department of Health, issued a boil w
local.body:
Fredonia doesn't need Halloween to scare itself. It has its water system -- newly slapped with yet another boil water order.

The Village of Fredonia Office of Emergency Management, in coordination with the village's water treatment plant and the Chautauqua County Department of Health, issued a boil water order at 8:45 a.m. today.

The stated reason was "High turbidity levels and treatment deficiencies." Fredonia was already under a water conservation order, caused by filtering challenges from at least two weeks of no rain.

Fredonia water customers should bring water to a rolling boil for at least one minute, then let it cool before using for drinking, cooking, brushing teeth, making ice, food preparation and washing produce, and preparing baby formula.

"The order will remain in place until testing confirms the water is safe," the Office of Emergency Management release stated. Boil orders typically last at least 48 hours, as a series of tests must be made and it takes a little time to get the results.

local.title: Rochester School for the Deaf celebrates 150 years
local.summary: The Rochester School for the Deaf is celebrating 150 years since it first opened. Alumni met with current students in the school library during celebrations.
local.body:
Listen • 1:08 The Rochester School for the Deaf is celebrating 150 years since it first opened.

Alumni met with current students in the school library during celebrations this month, and reminisced about what the school means to them decades after they graduated from the campus on St. Paul Street.

Patti Canne was among them. She graduated from Rochester School for the Deaf in 1981 and is now a social worker at the University of Rochester, working with deaf and hard of hearing patients.

Canne said in American Sign Language that returning to the school and connecting with current students is nostalgic.

"RSD is really my second home," Canne said through an interpreter. "I grew up here, I lived in the dorm, and it was just such a wonderful experience with all of the staff and the students and all of the support."

Growing up immersed in Deaf culture and language was significant, she said, and it's something she wants for future generations as well.

"Preserve Deaf schools," she said. "It's incredibly important for students to be at a Deaf school — for deaf students to be at a Deaf school — where they have full access to communication and language at all times."

The Rochester School for the Deaf provides state-funded, tuition-free, bilingual and bicultural education in American Sign Language and English for students from pre-Kindergarten through 21 years old, a school spokesperson said in a statement.

Margie Lynn Steiner Coran, 73, of Westfield, NY, formerly of Jeannette, PA, was lovingly embraced by Jesus, her Savior, at home with her husband by her side on Friday, October 23, 2026, following a recent illness. Born August 16, 1953, in Greensburg, PA, she was the daughter of the late Donald and Betty Wolfe Steiner.

A 1971 graduate of Penn Township High School, Margie earned an associate degree in business management from Westmoreland Community College, a bachelor's degree in elementary education from SUNY Fredonia, and a master's degree in elementary education and curriculum development from SUNY Oswego, graduating magna cum laude. She taught in the Liverpool and Ripley school districts before retiring in 2014. She was also a licensed cosmetologist and a devoted, supportive pastor's wife.

Margie was a member of Orchard Beach Assembly in North East, PA, where she participated in her Life Group. She also belonged to the Westfield Quilters Guild and was a beloved former Sunday school teacher at Lakeshore Assembly of God in Westfield.

An avid athlete and health enthusiast, Margie earned bronze, silver, and gold medals in the Chautauqua County Overland Ski Marathon in three consecutive years. She enjoyed gardening, golfing, exercising, skiing, playing pickleball, and biking with her husband and brother.

She is survived by her loving husband, Rev. Paul J. Coran, whom she married on November 18, 1978; her brother, Terry L. Steiner; her sister-in-law, Carol (Randy) Carper; her nephew, Dr. Ryan P. (Kristen) Carper, and their children, Brayden and Braxton; her niece, Erika (John) Glick, and their children, Ava, Addison, and Aiden; her aunts, Maryanne France and Carol Vargo; numerous cousins; and special friends Shaw Marie and Shauna Lee, who called her "Mom." In addition to her parents, she was preceded in death by her grandparents, several aunts, uncles, and cousins.

Family and friends will be received on Saturday, October 31, 2026, from 10 a.m. to noon at Orchard Beach Assembly, 2025 Orchard Beach Road, North East, PA 16428. A celebration of life will follow at noon, with Rev. Troy Keith officiating. A Private Committal will be held at the Vaia Funeral Home, Interment will be Twin Valley Memorial Park in Delmont, PA.

local.summary: On Lake Erie, the yellow perch fishing activity is kicking into high gear starting at 50-55 feet of water between Cattaraugus Creek and Sturgeon Point. Live emerald shiners fished near bottom is the top tactic if emeralds are available, but golden shiners or salted shiners are also effective. Angler
local.body:
On Lake Erie, the yellow perch fishing activity is kicking into high gear starting at 50-55 feet of water between Cattaraugus Creek and Sturgeon Point. Live emerald shiners fished near bottom is the top tactic if emeralds are available, but golden shiners or salted shiners are also effective. Anglers have also found the walleye stacked 20 feet thick in schools fishing at depths of 80-110 feet just west from Dunkirk to Barcelona. Paul Soper Jr. from the Northern Chautauqua Conservation Club recently shared that he limited out in 100 feet of water off Dunkirk with a three-man limit in two hours using stickbaits. Many of the fish were spitting up emerald shiners.

Did you put your boat away to head for the deer woods? Captain Daryl Glasner (716-462-8632) and Captain Tom Miranda (716-531-6683) are both still running perch and walleye trips from Sunset Bay at the Hanover Launch. Glasner is running musky trips to Chautauqua Lake, as well. So is Captain Mike Sperry (716-763-2947) at Chautauqua Reel Outdoors from Ashville Bay Marina. Sperry has been hooking up with Chautauqua Lake musky on a regular basis lately. All are very affordable.

With little rain recently, the steelhead are almost nill in the lower section of Cattaraugus Creek, which is running low and clear on most days. All the other tribs are at a trickle, too, and are practically void of fish. Shore anglers can be effective right now. Target steelhead from the Cattaraugus Creek breakwall or by wading off the tributary creek mouths and casting spoons and spinners. The mouth of Chautauqua Creek can be so good for low water casting periods like this. Boaters can score by trolling these creekmouth areas.

At the Lake Ontario piers at Wilson Harbor and Olcott Harbor, and in the Lower Niagara River, the salmon fishing is about ready to end. It's that time of year. Anglers are catching smallmouth bass, lake trout and steelhead in the lower river, both from the Devils Hole and Lewiston Landing areas from shore, and from the drift boaters.

For inland shore anglers, the DEC Randolph Fish Hatchery started its autumn stocking of broodstock trout three weeks ago. These trout are all over 2 years old and up to 30 inches long. The following waters have been stocked: Red House Lake with 130 rainbow trout and 200 brown trout; New Albion Lake with 50 brook trout, 50 rainbow trout and 150 brown trout; Case Lake with 25 brown trout, 100 rainbow trout and 400 brook trout; Genesee River with 200 brown trout and 250 rainbow trout; Quaker Lake with 200 brown trout and 300 rainbow trout; Lake Flavia with 100 brook trout, 250 brown trout and 50 rainbow trout; Allen Lake with 225 brook trout, 50 brown trout and 50 rainbow trout; Harwood Lake with 300 brook trout, 50 brown trout and 50 rainbow trout; Case Lake with 400 brook trout, 50 brown trout and 50 rainbow trout; Genesee River with 400 brown trout and 245 rainbow trout; and Cattaraugus Creek with 600 brown trout.

local.body:
Bernard Mount Jr. 66, of Jamestown NY, passed away October 22, 2026 after a long battle of cancer. He was born December 13, 1959 in Tampa FL to the parents of Bernard Mount Sr and Francis Mount.

Bernard was a beloved Father, grandparent, son, Uncle, friend of many who will be remembered for his spunky self, full of life, hardworking and someone you can always count on. He would have given anyone the shirt off of his back because that's just the type of person he was. Throughout his life he always enjoyed working, spending time with his kids, grandkids and great grandchildren. He also liked working on cars and helping people out. You could always count on him even when he didn't have much himself. He loved taking boat rides and just cruising around.

local.title: Letter to sports
local.summary: Dear Sports Editor: The Southern Tier lost a pillar of the wrestling community with the recent passing of Marty Rowe. local.body:
The Southern Tier lost a pillar of the wrestling community with the recent passing of Marty Rowe.

With the 1970s, came the beginning of the career of a young Mary Rowe on the Ripley wrestling team. By the end of his career, he had won many matches, had competed in the state tournament and, along the way, earned the respect of fellow wrestlers and coaches. By the time the 1980s had come around, the small school in southwestern Chautauqua County was competing and winning in Division 2 league competition, always against larger schools.

By the end of the 1980s, with the help of Coach John Carlton, the Ripley team was not only winning matches, but also claiming Division 2 titles and placing wrestlers during tournament competition, as well as the Section VI qualifier.

Soon, with the coaching aid of brother Darwin and nephews Brad and Ken, the team's winning ways continued with more dual-match victories, as well as tournament sectional titles. The team also saw more place finishes at the Section VI qualifier and the state tournament as well. It was during this period of time that the team was rewarded with its first individual state champion.

Soon thereafter, the team would merge with Chautauqua Lake, Clymer, Panama and Westfield to become known as the Eagles. They now compete with larger Division 1 schools, have continued their winning ways and have, to their credit, won multiple Division 1 titles and are now the class of their division.

Marty's influence on the wrestling community has indeed impacted many wrestlers through the years.

local.title: War on electric vehicles boomerangs on a nation
local.summary: Why on earth did Ford stop making its heralded electric truck? Ford stopped making the F-150 Lightning last December. There are several reasons Am
local.body:
Why on earth did Ford stop making its heralded electric truck? As Americans shudder at high gasoline prices, prospective truck buyers are lining up at car lots to buy used F-150 Lightning and other electric vehicles. Ford stopped making the F-150 Lightning last December.

There are several reasons American automakers pulled back from an earlier determination to enter the electric era with the rest of the world. And for their customers to be left to scrounge when energy prices revived demand. But the biggest reason is Donald Trump, and here’s an educated guess why he had it in for clean, renewable energy: money.

During the 2024 campaign, Trump pitched the fossil-fuel industry on a promise, since kept, to gut Joe Biden’s fuel-efficiency and climate rules. That helps explain why oil and gas interests poured $23 million into Trump’s reelection coffers, becoming his fourth biggest source of cash.

The Iran War has further raised energy prices, bringing more good news to certain bottom lines. As a recent Wall Street Journal headline put it, “American Oil Refiners Are Printing Money as Wars Shrink Global Energy Supplies.”

We’re not saying that Trump is waging war to help his contributors. What’s clear, however, is that by deep-sixing Biden’s campaign to reduce America’s dependency on fossil fuels, he left Americans vulnerable to the vagaries of their prices. Now he’s turning against Ukraine in its heroic fight against the Russian invasion, apparently to bring more Russian oil and gas back onto world markets. That could lower pump prices and, Trump hopes, save a few Republican seats in Congress.

How did second-term Trump try to kill off the American market for electric vehicles, putting domestic carmakers at a global disadvantage? Count the ways:

— In 2025, Trump pushed Republicans to end the $7,500 tax credit to buy EVs. Ford CEO Jim Farley said that the sharp drop in sales that followed was the main reason his company reconsidered its large EV investments. It’s also why General Motors scaled back, taking a $6 billion charge that included billions in canceled supplier contracts and settlements.

— He greatly weakened the fuel-economy standards for cars and trucks, which had pushed automakers to produce more energy-efficient vehicles.

local.title: Buffalo expands curbside composting program, aiming to serve 10,000 residents
local.summary: Buffalo is expanding its 'scrap-it' curbside composting program, aiming to serve 10,000 residents and keep more food waste out of landfills.
local.body: More Buffalo residents now have the chance to turn food waste into nutrient-rich compost, as the city expands its "scrap-it" curbside compost collection program to keep more food waste out of landfills.The weekly curbside pickup program has been piloted since 2023 for 2,000 single-family households across Buffalo, with 1.7 million pounds diverted from landfill in that time according to Terra Courtney, a worker owner at Farmer Pirates LLC which runs the program. "So that's a lot of food waste," Courtney said. Now, more Buffalonians will have the chance to take part."It'll be expanding from 2,000 hopefully to about 10,000 residents within the next five years," Courtney said. With 1,000 people on the waitlist, Courtney expects the first phase of the expansion to happen quickly. WATCH: Buffalo expands curbside composting program, aiming to serve 10,000 residentsOnce signed up, participants receive a brown 12 gallon tote which they fill with food scraps before placing it out on the curb for pickup each week along with their regular garbage and recycling totes.Farmer Pirates LLC handles curbside collection and brings the food scraps back to their headquarters on Buffalo's East Side where it is turned into compost over a period of six to eight months. The finished product is then sold to local farmers and gardeners each spring.Courtney listed some of the benefits of composting."This is a material that can be reused to rebuild our soils, to grow more food. If we send it to landfill there it's gonna slowly decay and potential release harmful methane into the atmosphere. Also landfills are not infinite they are taking up valuable space," Courtney explained.“Composting is a practical way for residents to make a difference in how much waste we send to landfills," Buffalo Mayor Sean Ryan said.The program will remain voluntary and on a first-come, first-served basis with a waiting list used to help ensure participation across the city. You can learn more and sign up at the Farmer Pirates LLC website. This story was reported on-air by a journalist and has been converted to this platform with the assistance of AI. local.title: 'I wanted to do a little dance': Repairs begin at deteriorating Depew Amtrak platform
local.summary: Repairs are underway at the Buffalo-Depew Amtrak station after a passenger who fell on the deteriorating platform raised concerns about its condition and what could happen to other travelers.
local.body: Repairs are underway at the Buffalo-Depew Amtrak station after a passenger who fell on the deteriorating platform raised concerns about its condition and what could happen to other travelers.Greg Rabb reached out to 7 News in September after he stumbled while stepping off an Amtrak train at the station.Rabb wasn't seriously hurt, but said he had been complaining about the deteriorating concrete for years.A month later, crews are now working on the platform.WATCH: 'I wanted to do a little dance': Repairs begin at deteriorating Depew Amtrak platform"I came up here just to look because I was thrilled," Rabb said. "I was so excited. I wanted to do a little dance."When 7 News first spoke with Rabb, he showed areas where the concrete was cracked and crumbling."You can see over here that that concrete is ready to collapse," Rabb said at the time. "I think this whole thing should be closed, but then you wouldn't have train service in Depew."Construction equipment was already at the station then, but work had not begun.7 News reached out to Amtrak, CSX and Congressman Tim Kennedy's office to find out what was preventing the repairs from moving forward.The holdup involved a "flagger" from CSX, which shares the tracks with Amtrak. A flagger was needed before construction could safely take place near the tracks. CSX said last month it was working to provide one.On Monday morning, Rabb returned to the station to pick up tickets for a trip later in the week and found crews at work."Miracle of miracles, I think in part because of what you're doing and what Channel 7 is doing and then the congressman's office, we finally got it going," Rabb said. "I'm really excited."A crew from Ideal Concrete was working to seal cracks in the platform, while a flagger was stationed nearby.The Buffalo-Depew station has a special connection to Rabb and his family. His father worked for New York Central and later Amtrak, and Rabb's family helped raise money for the buffalo statue in front of the station.For Rabb, however, getting the platform repaired is ultimately about making the station safer for everyone who uses it."I mean, it'll make it safer and nicer for everybody, and it'll make Buffalo look better when people come from out of town," he said.

entertainment.title: Amelia Dimoldenberg’s ‘Chicken Shop Date: The Final Series’ Will Hit Theaters for One Night Only
entertainment.summary: The show's final installment has been edited into a film, which will end with the last, unreleased 'Chicken Shop Date' episode.
entertainment.body:
Amelia Dimoldenberg ‘s Chicken Shop Date: The Final Series is coming to the big screen.

The YouTuber’s smash-hit interview show will play in theaters for one night only, in collaboration with the platform’s Cine Club, to mark the end of the series with avid fans.

All episodes of this last series will be brought together as “one cinematic experience,” featuring exclusive new material created especially for a larger screen. The film will culminate in the final, unreleased episode of Chicken Shop Date . Related Stories TV HBO's 'Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone' Casts James and Lily Potter, Charlie Weasley Movies David Bowie Returns to Berlin With Immersive Event

Ahead of the public screenings across 10 theaters in London and Paris, some invite-only premieres will take place in the British capital on Nov. 16 and in New York on Nov. 19. The film will then be presented to the public for one night only on Nov. 24 at select cinemas, before the final episode hits YouTube on Nov. 27.

The British writer and producer confirmed last month that the next season will be its last, bringing to a close the much-loved celebrity interview show she started as a teenager under the umbrella of her media company, Dimz Inc.

Dimoldenberg began Chicken Shop Date as a column when she was 17. The filmed series launched on YouTube in 2014 and has since grown into one of the internet’s most distinctive and celebrated interview formats, with Dimoldenberg “dating” stars across music, film, television and sport.

Some of its most memorable episodes feature Dave, Billie Eilish, Daniel Kaluuya, Central Cee, Andrew Garfield, Cher, Little Simz, Louis Theroux and Jack Harlow, as Dimoldenberg wielded her deadpan humor and the quintessential English setting of a local chicken shop to supposedly bolster her chances of finding love.

entertainment.title: Donnie Iris, ‘Ah! Leah!’ and ‘The Rapper’ Singer Dies at 83
entertainment.summary: The Pittsburgh favorite announced his retirement from performance just weeks ago after his final gig on Sept. 28.
entertainment.body:
Pittsburgh rocker Donnie Iris, best known for his 1981 No. 29 Billboard Hot 100 new wave hit “Ah! Leah!” and his 1970s Hot 100 No. 2 song “The Rapper” with the group the Jaggerz, has died at 83.

The news was shared by Donnie Iris & the Cruisers drummer Joe Vitale Jr., who wrote, “Tonight, I have some very sad news to share. Many of you may already know about this, but today my boss and friend Donnie Iris passed away at the age of 83,” in a Facebook post on Monday (Oct. 26). “At the first full show I performed with them in 2021, right before we went on stage, Donnie turned to me and gave me a huge hug. He always had an infectious smile, incredible energy and a wonderous personality. After you meet him, you honestly just love him. You could just sit and talk with him, laugh with him. He was King Cool.” No cause of death had been announced at press time.

A beloved staple of the Pittsburgh music scene, Elwood City native Iris was diagnosed with bladder cancer in 2023 shortly after his 80th birthday show, later canceling several shows and continuing to perform until announcing his retirement from the stage earlier this month after a final gig at Citizens Live at The Wylie in Pittsburg on Sept. 28.

“After much thought, and in light of recent health issues, I have made the difficult decision to retire from future concert performances,” Iris wrote on Oct. 9. “Music has given me far more than I could ever put into words. From the earliest days to every chapter of my life, your support has been a constant source of joy and inspiration.”

Dominic Ierace was born on Feb. 28, 1943 in New Castle, Pa., and got his start in grade school singing at weddings and talent contests. The man who would grow up to be dubbed Pittsburgh’s King Cool of Rock and Roll first played with the doo-wop group The Fabutons in high school, then with the R&B/rock cover bands the Tri-Vels and Donnie and the Donnells while at Slippery Rock State College, before dropping out to pursue a music career. He found success pretty quickly with “The Rapper” from his group The Jaggerz, a swinging rock tune about a smooth-talking dude who uses a series of smarmy lines to pick up women at bars. The song he recorded for Gamble Records (formed by future Philly soul legends producers/songwriters Kenny Gamble and Leon Huff) for the band’s sophomore album, 1970’s We Went to Different Schools Together , rose all the way to No. 2 on the Billboard Hot 100.

entertainment.title: Kordell Stewart Hopes His New HBO Documentary Lands Him in the NFL Hall of Fame
entertainment.summary: 'Kordell Stewart: Slash & Burn' from Skydance Sports tackles the gay rumor that the former Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback says derailed his career.
entertainment.body:
Kordell Stewart wants you to watch new HBO short documentary Kordell Stewart: Slash & Burn ( Skydance Sports , NFL Films ), digest its contents, and then reconsider his professional football career. If you’re feeling especially generous — and if you happen to have a vote — the “Slash” of Slash & Burn would also like to be considered for the Pro Football Hall of Fame, please and thank you.

In 1995, Stewart came out of the University of Colorado with a cannon for an arm, the foot speed and hands of a wideout, and the promise of a whole new prototype: a true running quarterback. (And oh yeah, one “Miracle at Michigan” under his belt. )

“Randall Cunningham brought awareness to the mobile quarterback,” Stewart, who was drafted 60th overall that year by the Pittsburgh Steelers, told The Hollywood Reporter . “I like to say I tore the hinges off the door.”

He did. Stewart was a true phenomenon, a star both on the field and in one of the best forgotten sneaker-chain ad campaigns of all time. (The commercial kids about it, but Stewart actually was the team’s backup punter — and an effective one at times .)

Stewart’s 1997 season, his first as the Steelers’ starting QB, was explosive with 32 combined passing and rushing touchdowns. In 2001, Stewart made the Pro Bowl and finished fourth in the league’s MVP voting. And then the rumor happened.

To this day, no one knows who started it, but Stewart’s camp believes it originated from within the Pittsburgh Police Department. The rumor alleged that Stewart was caught and arrested for engaging in a lewd act with another man in a local park. But here’s the thing: the arrest never happened and the rumor, investigated by the Steelers organization, was never substantiated. Though Stewart denied then and denies now that the act ever took place, the idea that the Steel City’s star quarterback was gay lingered in the mid-90s blue-collar town. It was a major distraction to say the least, Stewart says.

His career was never the same. Stewart would soon lose his starting job and bounce to the Chicago Bears (and lose that starting job), until ultimately finishing his football life as a backup for the Baltimore Ravens. It was a real “What-could-have-been?” NFL tenure. (One thing legendary Steelers coach Bill Cowher says could have been is Stewart could have been a Hall of Fame wide receiver if he switched positions earlier and committed; Stewart concurs.)
