entertainment.title: Ariana Grande Shines Brighter Than a Christmas Tree in Luxury Brand’s Musical Holiday Spectacular Campaign Video
entertainment.summary: Swarovski has unveiled its latest collaboration with the singer.
entertainment.body:
Who needs Christmas tree ornaments when you’ve already got all the sparkle you need? Ariana Grand e raises the question through her shimmering new Swarovski holiday musical campaign, which the iconic jewelry brand unveiled Tuesday (Oct. 27).

Soundtracked by a theatrical orchestral arrangement that switches back and forth between jazzy and classical styles, the minute-long video opens with the pop star in a white suit and top hat, outfitted with many silver gems and brooches. She then leads a group of similarly dapper-looking backup dancers in a routine on a grand staircase before the scene switches to Grande in a princess gown surrounded by pink feathers.

Other scenes in the sequence show Grande poking her head inside a festive dollhouse to hand a present to its miniature residents and channeling her inner ballerina in a Swan Lake -inspired sequence. At the end, the video cuts to the Wicked actress watching the ad in a theater, cheering as the credits roll before winking at the camera.

Grande has been the face of Swarovski since July 2024 and has starred in a number of seasonal campaigns for the brand, including visuals for Valentine’s Day, summer and one called “Ariana Grande’s Fantasy Garden Comes to Life.” “I cannot wait to embark on this journey and to inspire others to embrace their own unique sparkle,” she stated when the partnership was first announced.

The Grammy winner is currently on a break from the public eye since the conclusion of her Eternal Sunshine Tour in September. Her rep announced she’d be taking time away from the spotlight in August amid a spike in public scrutiny stemming from her physical appearance in the “Petal” music video. Billboard later confirmed that Grande still planned to do promo for her upcoming film, Focker-in-Law , as well as her brands, including R.E.M. Beauty.

entertainment.title: ‘Fair Play’ Doc About Olympic Gymnast Jordan Chiles Set for 2027 Release on Hulu, Disney+ (Exclusive)
entertainment.summary: Andscape is behind director Trishtan Williams' feature about the athlete who helped lead Team USA to Olympic gold in 2024.
entertainment.body:
A feature documentary about Olympic gymnast Jordan Chiles is getting ready to roll.

Andscape has began production on Fair Play: The Jordan Chiles Story from filmmaker Trishtan Williams ( Starting 5 ), The Hollywood Reporter has learned. The film is set to be released on Hulu and Hulu on Disney+ in fall of 2027 amid the lead-up to the 2028 Olympic Games in Los Angeles .

Fair Play: The Jordan Chiles Story offers unprecedented access to the 25-year-old gymnast who faces a pivotal moment in life. Chiles helped Team USA take silver at the 2020 Tokyo Olympic Games before helping lead the team to gold at the 2024 Olympics in Paris. Hailing from Andscape, Campfire Studios and Select Entertainment, the documentary will show Chiles inside the gym and out as she navigates life in the spotlight as a voice for a new generation of athletes. Related Stories Business The NFL's Biggest Dramas This Season Are In the Broadcast Booth TV Hulu's Rumored Clavicular Doc Is Actually a True-Crime Series (Exclusive)

Producers include Ross M. Dinerstein and Allyson Holloway for Campfire Studios. Executive producing are Anne Hazlett for Campfire Studios, alongside Lisa Filipelli, Amy Neben and Alexia Maitland for Select Entertainment.

Williams’ previous directorial credits include the first two seasons of Netflix’s Starting 5 , along with Life in the W for ESPN and Why Not Us: Howard Golf , with the latter counting Stephen Curry as executive producer. Other television credits include Love Is Blind , America’s Next Top Model and The Amazing Race.

Chiles’ career highlights include her accomplishment in 2022 of becoming one of three Black gymnasts to sweep the podium at the U.S. Championships. She has become a best-selling author with memoir I’m That Girl , finished third on last year’s Dancing With the Stars and established herself as an advocate for mental health and body positivity.

“My journey in gymnastics has taught me a lot about resilience, perseverance, and the importance of defining success on my own terms,” says Chiles. “As I work toward LA28, I’m excited to partner with Andscape and Hulu to share more of my story, reflect on the experiences that have shaped me, and explore what it means to step into this next chapter while reclaiming my narrative.”

Adds Williams, “Jordan is so much more than an extraordinary athlete. She’s a young woman navigating immense expectations while finding the courage to define herself on her own terms. What excites me most about directing this film is the opportunity to capture Jordan in all her dimensions — her joy, vulnerability, ambition, and resilience. With unprecedented access, this doc goes beyond medals and competition to explore identity, purpose, and what it truly means to take back the pen and write your own story.”

entertainment.title: 50 Cent Sues Rick Ross Ex in $6M Defamation Lawsuit Over ‘Offensive’ Posts About Teenage Son
entertainment.summary: The star has launched coast-to-coast legal actions against Tia Kemp over ugly social media posts about his son Sire Jackson.
entertainment.body:
50 Cent is suing Rick Ross ‘ ex-girlfriend over “highly offensive” social media posts about his 14-year-old son, including “sexually degrading” insults and a “fabricated medical diagnosis.”

In a lawsuit Monday (Oct. 26) in Los Angeles federal court, attorneys for the rapper (Curtis Jackson) accuse Tiallondra “Tia” Kemp of defamation over her posts last week about Sire Jackson, in which she claimed he had autism due to conduct by his mother, Daphne Joy, when she was pregnant with him.

“Ms. Kemp shamelessly used the label ‘on the spectrum’ as a pejorative slur hurled at a child to humiliate him and his family. But autism is not shameful,” 50 Cent’s lawyers write. “What is shameful is fabricating a diagnosis for a private child, inventing a sexually degrading cause for it, and broadcasting both to a mass audience.”

The star’s lawyers say the offensive comments, under an Instagram photo of Sire and his parents, were made as part of an effort “to settle a score with his father” via a “a mass-audience campaign of falsehood and sexual degradation.”

“This action arises from a grown adult’s deliberate decision to use a young child as a prop and a punchline in order to wound the child’s father,” 50 Cent’s lawyers write. “S.J. is a minor and not a public figure.”

Monday’s federal lawsuit, obtained and first reported by Billboard , builds on a case filed earlier that day in Florida court, in which 50 accused Kemp of cyberstalking and harassing Sire. That case, which also seeks a restraining order, was first reported by TMZ.

According to the new California lawsuit, the full caption under Kemp’s original post of Sire and his mother read: “Btchhhh azzzz @50cent U wanna play? U have NO room to post anyone’s child when urs on the spectrum and the reason being this hoooo was still swallowing 10,000 gallons of CUMMM when she was pregnant.”

Kemp’s comments appear to have been in response to posts earlier this month in which 50 Cent trolled Ross over an alleged assault on his 21-year-old son, whom he shares with Kemp. The rapper posted an image of the suspected assailant’s mugshot and joked that he would bail him out.

entertainment.title: BET Revamps the Soul Train Awards: ‘We Knew This Couldn’t Be a Granddaddy’ Show
entertainment.summary: Following a two-year hiatus, the awards franchise will air on Nov. 27.
entertainment.body:
When the Soul Train Awards return on Nov. 27 after a two-year hiatus, BET president Louis Carr is promising viewers one thing. “We knew this couldn’t be a granddaddy Soul Train,” he tells Billboard . “We knew we had to celebrate the past — but also introduce the future of R&B.”

With that in mind, this year’s Soul Train Awards will feature only two fan-voted categories: R&B/Soul Song of the Year, with voting on BET.com and Spotify’s RNB X International Artist, with voting in the Spotify app. The revamped format for the two-hour show will also be comprised of tributes to three special artist honorees representing Classic Soul, New Soul and Soul Personified. Chaka Khan was recently announced as the 2026 recipient of the Classic Soul Honor. On Tuesday (Oct. 27), it was revealed that Durand Bernarr will be presented with the Soul Personified Honor.

“We’ve learned over the last couple of years that finding a bridge for the generations is important as is honoring [legacies],” explains BET executive vp, specials, music programming & music strategy, Connie Orlando , who joined Carr for Billboard ’s Zoom interview. “People miss that and really gravitate toward it. In addition to Classic Soul, we’ll have a New Soul award honoring someone who is super-hot right now. And we’ll have a Soul Personified award for an artist who’s hitting on all cylinders and personifies soul music.”

The New Soul honoree, as well as the performer lineup, will be revealed in the coming weeks. Two show staples will also return. One is the Soul Cypher, which featured Marsha Ambrosius, Eric Bellinger, Nicci Gilbert and Arin Ray when the Soul Train Awards last aired in 2023. The second is the BET Amplified Stage, which showcases emerging artists. The 2023 show spotlighted October London and Honey Bxby on the Amplified Stage.

entertainment.title: Turnpike Troubadours Earn First Hot 100 Hit With Zach Bryan Collab ‘Plainsman’
entertainment.summary: The song by the Oklahoman acts is from Bryan’s Young Manhood and Other Donatable Organs .
entertainment.body:
Turnpike Troubadours land their first career entry on the Billboard Hot 100 , thanks to the group’s featured appearance on Zach Bryan’s “Plainsman.”

The track, from Bryan’s new eight-song set, Young Manhood and Other Donatable Organs (released Oct. 16 via Belting Bronco/Warner Records), launches at No. 45 on the chart dated Oct. 31 almost entirely from streaming. It earned 6 million official U.S. streams in the Oct. 16-22 tracking week, according to Luminate, along with nearly 1,000 downloads sold. Related Ryan Gosling's Dead Man's Bones Duo Creep Back With Romantic 'Lost in the Night' Video Starring Noah Jupe and Rain Spencer Taylor Swift, George Strait, Lee Thomas Miller & More Celebrated During Nashville Songwriters Hall of Fame Gala Disturbed to Play 'The Sickness' in Full on Australia and New Zealand Tour Explore Zach Bryan See latest videos, charts and news

“Plainsman” also arrives at No. 14 on both the Hot Country Songs and Hot Rock & Alternative Songs charts, likewise giving Turnpike Troubadours their first appearance on each ranking.

Cowritten by Bryan and Turnpike Troubadours frontman Evan Felker, “Plainsman” marks the first recording between the two Oklahoma acts. Bryan is famously a longtime fan of the group. On his 2023 song “East Side of Sorrow,” he nodded to the band’s reunion and its first album in six years, singing, “I heard Turnpike’s back together and they’re writin’ songs.” The group went on to open for Bryan on select dates of his Quittin’ Time Tour in 2024.

Until now, Turnpike Troubadours’ chart success had come largely on the album side. The band has charted five titles on the Billboard 200 , Top Country Albums and Americana/Folk Albums charts, with four reaching the top 10 of the lattermost list, including 2017’s No. 1, A Long Way From Your Heart .

The group’s first appearance on a Billboard songs chart came last year, when “Heaven Passing Through,” from its latest LP, The Price of Admission , debuted on Country Airplay. The single peaked at No. 46 this March over a 33-week run on the chart.

As for Bryan, Young Manhood and Other Donatable Organs debuts at No. 2 on the Billboard 200 with 65,000 equivalent album units earned. It also opens at No. 1 on Top Country Albums, Top Rock Albums and Americana/Folk Albums, giving him his fifth No. 1 on all three charts.

entertainment.title: How KATSEYE’s Sophia Laforteza Made ‘Forgotten Island’ INXS Cover Her Own: ‘She Really Has the Story in Her DNA’
entertainment.summary: Go inside Sophia's version of "Never Tear Us Apart" in this bonus feature from the DreamWorks Animation film's digital debut.
entertainment.body:
With Forgotten Island ‘s central story of friendship and themes inspired by Philippines mythology, Filipino-American singer Sophia Laforteza of the global girl group KATSEYE was a fitting pick to make music for the DreamWorks Animation film.

In a new digital bonus feature debuting exclusively on Billboard , Sophia and her collaborators — including composer Nathan Matthew David, producer Mike Elizondo and writers/directors Joel Crawford and Januel P. Mercado — take viewers inside the studio to discuss the making of her cover of INXS’ “Never Tear Us Apart” for the film, which arrives on digital platforms Tuesday (Oct. 27) with more than 60 minutes of bonus content.

“‘Never Tear Us Apart’ is really kind of the journey of this movie and of the girls’ friendship – their anthem, in a way,” Crawford says of lead besties Raissa and Jo (voiced by singer/songwriter H.E.R.).

“For Sophia and Mike and Nathan to make it an interpretation that stands on its own is an incredible accomplishment,” Mercado adds of reinterpreting the 1988 top 10 Billboard Hot 100 hit for INXS.

For David, Sophia immediately impressed him in the studio. “Right from the beginning of her vocal session, we knew it was going to be really special. I think she just sang the hell out of this song.”

Sophia’s personal connection to the film as a Filipino American was what drove home the musical connection. “Hearing her talk about how she really has the story in her DNA, in her soul — what she brought to this, I can’t imagine anyone else,” Crawford says.

That story was Sophia’s north star as she navigated making “Never Tear Us Apart” her own. “As a performer, my strength is, if you tell me what the story is, I’ll tell it the best way that I can,” she says in the bonus feature. “I got to watch the scene while singing it, and I really tried to take every ounce of knowledge I knew just growing up in this world. This is one of the most beautiful things I think I’ll ever do.”

Sophia is currently on hiatus from KATSEYE, but HYBE announced earlier this month that she plans to return to group activities in January 2027. She stepped back from the group in August to focus on her mental health, meaning she’ll miss the full Wildworld Tour, which wraps up at the end of November after a planned 31 arena shows across Europe and North America.

entertainment.title: Susan Saint James, ‘Name of the Game,’ ‘McMillan & Wife’ and ‘Kate & Allie’ Star, Dies at 80
entertainment.summary: The Emmy winner (and eight-time nominee) also worked in such films as ‘Love at First Bite,’ ‘How to Beat the High Cost of Living’ and ‘Carbon Copy.’
entertainment.body:
Susan Saint James, the Emmy-winning actress who delighted TV viewers with her light-hearted turns on The Name of the Game , McMillan & Wife and Kate & Allie before quitting at the peak of her powers, has died. She was 80.

Saint James died Monday of pancreatic cancer, her family announced.

Survivors include her third husband, Dick Ebersol, the former Saturday Night Live executive producer and head of NBC Sports whom she married in November 1981. The couple soldiered on after losing their youngest child, 14-year-old son Teddy, in a 2004 plane crash. Related Stories Movies Hubert de la Bouillerie, 'Woodstock' and 'Witches of Eastwick' Film Editor, Dies at 75 TV Alan Dysert, 'All My Children' Actor, Dies at 75

Saint James was someone who was “generous with her time and energy, which she valued more than money, and instinctively drawn to whoever needed lifting up,” her family said. “She taught her children to pause, be kind and look out for other people.”

On the big screen, she went on the run with Peter Fonda in Outlaw Blues (1977); played the lustful target of Dracula in Love at First Bite (1979), starring George Hamilton; executed a heist with fellow suburbanites Jessica Lange and Jane Curtin in How to Beat the High Cost of Living (1980); and portrayed George Segal ’s wife in Carbon Copy (1981).

A contract player at Universal, Saint James portrayed the frequently kidnapped editorial assistant Peggy Maxwell for three seasons (1968-71) on the stylish 90-minute NBC drama The Name of the Game . ( THR took a look back at the series in 2018).

Peggy worked at Howard Publications for all three of the rotating characters on the “wheel” series — Tony Franciosa as hotshot reporter Jeff Dillon, Gene Barry as kingly publisher Glenn Howard and Robert Stack as FBI agent turned magazine editor Dan Farrell.

Six months after The Name of the Game ’s final episode, Saint James was back on another 90-minute wheel series, McMillan & Wife , which began in rotation with Columbo and McCloud as part of the NBC Mystery Movie franchise.

entertainment.title: The NFL’s Biggest Dramas This Season Are In the Broadcast Booth
entertainment.summary: From Troy Aikman to Tony Romo, the on-air talent who function as the gateway to the game have become the story, much to the league's chagrin.
entertainment.body:
The NFL might be the undisputed king of TV content, but it is off-the-field drama that has dominated much of the conversation around the game this season so far.

In particular, it was a widely reported altercation before the Los Angeles Rams-Buffalo Bills game at SoFi Stadium earlier this month … in the ESPN broadcast booth.

To recap: ESPN’s lead play-by-play announcer Joe Buck signed a rich new contract with the company, but his longtime analyst partner Troy Aikman has not, resulting in reported bad blood between the boothmates.

On-air, of course, viewers would have no clue (Buck and Aikman have continued to deliver a broadcast worthy of their decamillion dollar contracts), but the dispute has become fodder, and Aikman has not been willing to shy away from discussing it.

The former Dallas Cowboys quarterback appeared on The Mike Fisher Show on Friday, where he was almost melancholy about what his future holds in media.

“I never had any interest in going into television, it was just by happenstance that I even got into it,” Aikman said, recalling the outreach from Fox Sports . “I don’t know that if they hadn’t hired me, I would have gotten an opportunity anywhere else. And here I am, 25 years later, and now as I’m into my last year at ESPN, I’m realizing that this is something that could very well be taken away from me, and so for the first time, I’m realizing how much I really do, and I’ve always enjoyed it.

“Until you risk having something taken away from you, I think sometimes you tend to maybe take things for granted,” he continued. “And so for the first time probably in my career, I’m realizing, you know, this is a great profession, it’s been a great ride for me, and I hope that it’s not over.”

As the faces of Fox and ESPN’s NFL coverage, Aikman and Buck have been staples on Sundays (and more recently Mondays) for years. The looming end of that is ripping through sports, media and the league itself. And the situation comes as Disney is set to host its first Super Bowl since 2006, with Buck and Aikman set to lead the game from the booth (they have also been a big part of its marketing). But with their rich deals, nothing can be assured, and in the TV business, any opportunity to get a better deal or sign talent that could make a difference is typically taken fast.

entertainment.title: ‘Babel’: THR’s 2006 Review
entertainment.summary: On Oct. 27, 2006, Paramount unveiled Alejandro González Iñárritu's drama in theaters following its premiere in competition at the Cannes Film Festival.
entertainment.body:
On Oct. 27, 2006, Paramount unveiled Alejandro González Iñárritu’s Babel in theaters following its premiere in competition at the Cannes Film Festival in May. The feature, starring Brad Pitt, Cate Blanchett and Gael Garcia Bernal, was nominated for seven Oscars at the 79th Academy Awards, including best picture. It walked away with one win, in the original score category. The Hollywood Reporter’s original review is below:

Tense, relentless and difficult to watch at times, Alejandro González Iñárritu’s Babel is an emotionally shattering drama in which a simple act of kindness leads to events that pierce our veneer of civilization and bring on the white noise of terror.

Iñárritu and screen writer Guillermo Arriaga involve six families, most of them not known to one another, in four countries on three continents in their story of random fate and the perils of being unable to communicate.

Brad Pitt, Cate Blanchett and Gael Garcia Bernal give committed ensemble performances alongside seasoned character performers and nonactors as the story ranges from Morocco to San Diego to Tokyo.

The film, which also features exceptional work by director of photography Rodrigo Prieto, production designer Brigitte Broch, editors Stephen Mirrione and Douglas Crise and composer Gustavo Santaolalla, is headed for major prizes and large, appreciative audiences.

As with his previous films, Iñárritu tells his story using scenes out of order so that the pieces fall together in a jagged form that heightens the tension. It starts in the Moroccan desert, where a man buys a Winchester rifle from a neighbor to help keep the jackals away from his herd of goats. A Japanese hunter had gifted the neighbor with the rifle in gratitude for his work as a guide.

The rifle is entrusted to the goat herder’s two young sons, who end up firing it from a mountainside at a coach filled with Western tourists just to see how far the bullet would go.

The bullet, however, strikes an American named Susan (Blanchett) who is traveling with her husband Richard (Pitt) in attempt to patch up their marriage following the death of a child.

entertainment.title: David Bowie Returns to Berlin With Immersive Event
entertainment.summary: Documentary filmmaker Brett Morgen ('Moonage Daydream') will present 'Stage,' an immersive concert experience designed around recently discovered Bowie tour footage, at the 2027 Berlinale.
entertainment.body:
Oscar-nominated documentary filmmaker Brett Morgen ( Moonage Daydream , On the Ropes ) will present the world premiere of Stage , his new immersive David Bowie concert experience, at the 2027 Berlinale .

Morgen designed the immersive concert around original camera footage from Bowie’s 1978 Isolar II World Tour, which the director discovered while doing research for his 2022 documentary on Bowie, Moonage Daydream . The tour features Bowie performing material from Heroes , the landmark album he wrote and recorded while living in Berlin. Like Moonage Daydream , Stages was created with the cooperation of the David Bowie Estate. Bowie, a genre- and gender-bending icon of pop music , and one of biggest rock stars in history, died in 2016 , aged 69. Related Stories TV HBO's 'Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone' Casts James and Lily Potter, Charlie Weasley Business Hilary Rosen Named BAFTA Chair

Stages features a three-screen presentation combining large-scale projections of the recovered and restored footage alongside transparent LED screens and a lighting design from Patrick Woodroffe, who has lit and designed tours for everyone from ABBA and The Police to Adele and Michael Jackson. He also lit Martin Scorsese’s Rolling Stones’ concert documentary Shine a Light , which opened the Berlinale in 2006.

Paul Massey, the Academy Award-winning sound mixer of Bohemian Rhapsody (and 11-time Oscar nominee), created a special sound mix for Stages to give the audience the experience of being at the center of a live David Bowie concernt.

Stages will have its world premiere at Berlin’s Uber Arena on Feb. 14, on the first weekend of the Berlinale.

Berlinale director Tricia Tuttle called the event “a dream come true” for the festival. “The Berlinale is a place where cinema, art, and new forms of storytelling intersect,” she said. “To have this world premiere [of Stages ] in Berlin, a city so closely connected to David Bowie, makes the experience especially meaningful.”

Morgen was Oscar-nominated for his 1999 boxing documentary On The Ropes and has directed several acclaimed docs, including Cobain: Montage of Heck (2015), on Kurt Cobain, the Emmy-winning Jane (2017) on the primatologist Jane Goodall, and The Kid Stays in the Picture (2002), on legendary Paramount producer Robert Evans.

Morgen will attend the Berlinale and be a headline contributor to the European Film Market’s talks program.

entertainment.title: Hilary Rosen Named BAFTA Chair
entertainment.summary: Formerly deputy chair of the Academy, Rosen replaces the outgoing Sara Putt.
entertainment.body:
Hilary Rosen has been promoted to BAFTA chair, succeeding Sara Putt.

Putt steps down after a three-year term, with her deputy stepping up to fill the role. Rosen will oversee BAFTA’s mission to champion film, games and television talent through its awards, industry leadership and year-round development programs.

A BAFTA Television Committee member since 2021 and later its chair, Rosen helped shape the TV and Craft Awards and oversee their juries, according to the British film and TV academy. Outside of BAFTA, Rosen is director of commissioning at UKTV, leading its slate of original scripted and unscripted content.

She’ll be supported by Ade Rawcliffe and Andrew Miller as deputy chairs of the Academy. They’ll both serve a two-year term.

And after a thorough election process, the following have been appointed to the Board of Trustees: Charu Desodt and Caroline Levy are the new Chairs for BAFTA’s Games and Television Committees, while Nahrein Kemp will take up the role of LIT Committee Chair. Shrina Shah, chair of the governance and appointments committee, will join the BAFTA Board of Trustees.

Rosen described the promotion as “a great privilege.” She continued: “I have long been passionate about everything BAFTA does to promote the screen arts and champion talent across the screen industries… I am delighted to be able to do this alongside our newly appointed committee chairs, Charu, Caroline and Nahrein and the rest of the BAFTA Board of Trustees. All are outstanding industry leaders, and with the collective passion and insight we share, I’m confident that this Board of Trustees will continue to build on the important and impactful work that has gone before.”

entertainment.title: ‘The One About Matthew Perry’ Review: Netflix’s Intimate and Sincere but Overly Padded Docuseries
entertainment.summary: Perry's sister Mia and various friends, former girlfriends and colleagues talk about the actor's genius and his demons in Mary Robertson's three-parter.
entertainment.body:
Logo text Perhaps it’s most helpful to begin a discussion of Netflix ‘s three-part The One About Matthew Perry with an acknowledgment of the things that it is not.

Directed by Mary Robertson ( Quiet on Set: The Dark Side of Kids TV ), The One About Matthew Perry is not a salacious documentary about Perry’s death and the subsequent criminal investigations. Peacock already did one of those, and if you skipped it, you’re better off. The One About Matthew Perry The Bottom Line A fine feature-length doc unnecessarily extended into a three-hour docuseries. Airdate: Tuesday, October 27 (Netflix) Director: Mary Robertson

The One About Matthew Perry also isn’t a definitive celebration of the life and comic genius of Matthew Perry, as related by those who worked with him most closely. Related Stories Business Netflix Hires Former Apple Exec Steve Wilson to Lead Podcast Acquisitions Business Ted Sarandos Swoops Into Seoul as Netflix Celebrates 10 Years in Korea

That is to say, it’s not a documentary designed to spawn “10 Fun Things We Learned From…” listicles and — despite the pandering title, with its borrowing of Friends episodic nomenclature — it’s only a documentary about Matthew Perry and his hit NBC sitcom insofar as you can’t tell Perry’s story without reciting nostalgic talking points about Friends . Even if it might be better if you could.

Literally none of Perry’s Friends co-stars appear in the documentary — nope, not even Janice or Gunther — nor do any of the key creative forces from the show. Unless you count Warren Littlefield, NBC’s entertainment president at the time, as a creative force from the show. Otherwise, one writer from the first season (Jeff Strauss) is included, but nobody with a high enough profile is there to say anything that might be interpreted as sensational or sensationalistic.

The same is roughly true of the rest of the A-listers whom Perry worked with over the years. Fools Rush In is represented by producer Doug Draizin, Studio 60 on the Sunset Strip (and Mr. Sunshine ) by Nate Torrence, The Whole Nine Yards by director Jonathan Lynn.

I can’t say whether or not Robertson reached out to the various big names in Perry’s celebrity sphere, but it’s my instinct both that she did not and that none of them would have agreed to participate anyway. The bigger the names you get, the more the focus of the documentary becomes what Lisa Kudrow or David Schwimmer or Aaron Sorkin have to say about Matthew Perry, rather than Matthew Perry.
